regions.full_page: Yes, my coming hither to St. Michael's has been a decided re- lief to me from the continued drain and strain of difficulties brought to the office for twenty years at St. Bonaventure's in Detroit. I do have perhaps as long hours but its a change. Here its correspondence takes most of my time. There, I simply had to leave most of that to others; and while I meet with pathetic cases to solve or try to aleviate the strain and tension is by no means so pressing. In brief conclusion of this page, I wish you would make a special memento for a couple of problems I have been working on without the progress I'd be encouraged to see. "Better late than never", Answered Joe Ferbush working on the roof of the "new granery" down on the Burkhardt farm when I called him to supper, lamenting tardiness. So, while to have thanked you in the beginning for your charitable interest and faith in the Seraphic Mass Association together with the welfare of our dear ones in estrangement from the ways of peace .... I'll do so now; while, this time at least, I shall prepare certificates according- ly, etc. Hoping that you may, without too much trouble supply my skip- ping and slipping in the course of the above and with best regards and God's blessing to Father Maurice Joachim, Father Klein, and Father Harrington and all our friends you may chance to meet, I hope to remain, of service to you and your good work etc,

regions.full_page: P.S. Dear Monsignor E'd. I thought it over and have made out the inclosed card .... I figure the poor fellow "got his foot in it ( very likely) without realizing its danger. If you think it advisable to send it to him or should you prefer me to do so, you could return it and give me M M's Ad.
